setup: You work as {role|a} at {workplace|a}, where the guide asks staff to use materials, water and energy responsibly.
As {role|a} at {workplace|a}, you follow a guide for using resources responsibly.
detail: It is the middle of the afternoon.
pressure: {coworker3} says it is not worth the trouble.
You are in a hurry to finish.

tiers.1: Chemicals that reach a drain can harm people and the environment.
tiers.2: A running leak wastes water every minute it continues.
tiers.3: Sorting materials lets them be recycled instead of buried.
tiers.4: Empty rooms do not need power.
tiers.5: Reusing clean material saves resources but can wait behind urgent problems.

fact: You have leftover cleaning solution, and the guide says only trained staff handle chemical waste using its labeled, compatible containers.
issues.action: Keep it secured and ask trained staff to handle it under the guide.
issues.brief: ask trained staff to handle the secured chemical waste
issues.reason: The guide assigns disposal to trained staff who know the product and its compatible waste container.
issues.lesson: Follow product-specific disposal instructions and use trained staff; do not mix or rinse chemicals on your own.

shortcut.text: Rinse it down the sink with plenty of water so it is diluted.
shortcut.why: Dilution does not stop the chemicals from reaching the drain, and the guide names the waste container.
shortcut.mis: Plenty of water makes any chemical harmless.

clear: Trained staff have already taken responsibility for the secured leftover solution.
issues.done: trained staff are handling the leftover solution

fact: A faucet in the supply room is dripping steadily, and the guide says leaks are reported to maintenance.
issues.action: Report the leak to maintenance so it can be repaired.
issues.reason: A steady drip adds up to a lot of wasted water, and maintenance has the tools to repair it.
issues.lesson: Report leaks so they are fixed, instead of living with the waste.

shortcut.text: Tighten it a bit yourself and move on, since it is only a drip.
shortcut.brief: tighten it yourself and move on
shortcut.why: A quick tightening may not fix the leak, and the guide says maintenance repairs leaks.
shortcut.mis: A small drip is not worth reporting.

clear: Maintenance already has a report about the dripping faucet.

fact: You have a stack of used cardboard, and the workplace has a labeled bin for cardboard across the room.
issues.action: Flatten the cardboard and put it in the cardboard bin.
issues.brief: flatten it and use the cardboard bin
issues.reason: Cardboard in the right bin can be recycled, and flattening saves space for more.
issues.lesson: Sort recyclable materials into the right bin, even when it takes a few steps.

shortcut.text: Put it in the trash, since the cardboard bin is across the room.
shortcut.why: Cardboard in the trash is wasted, and the bin is only a few steps away.
shortcut.mis: The trash is close enough for anything.

clear: The used cardboard was already flattened and put in the bin.

fact: The guide says to turn off lights and equipment in empty rooms, and you are the last person leaving this room.
issues.short: the lights and equipment left on
issues.action: Turn off the lights and equipment before you leave.
issues.brief: turn off the lights and equipment
issues.reason: Power used in an empty room does no work, and it takes only a moment to stop.
issues.lesson: Switch off lights and equipment when you are the last to leave.

shortcut.text: Leave everything on in case someone comes back.
shortcut.why: Power used in an empty room is wasted, and anyone returning can switch it on.

clear: The lights and equipment in the room were already switched off.
issues.done: the room is already switched off

fact: Packing material from a delivery is clean, and the guide says reusable material is kept for shipping.
issues.action: Set the clean packing material aside in the reuse area.
issues.reason: Reusing clean packing saves buying new material and keeps it out of the trash.
issues.lesson: Keep clean, reusable material for the next job.

shortcut.text: Throw it away to keep the area tidy.
shortcut.why: The guide keeps reusable material for shipping, and throwing it out means buying more.
shortcut.mis: A tidy area matters more than reuse.

proceed.text: Carry on with your regular work, since nothing here needs action.
proceed.why: Each of these situations involves materials, water or energy that need a responsible response.
proceed.lesson: Using resources responsibly means putting each material where the guide says and not wasting what runs or burns.

generic.text: Ask {coworker2} what they usually do and copy that.
generic.why: A coworker's habit is not the written guide, and it may be out of date.
generic.mis: Common practice is the same as the rule.

generic.text: Wait until {lead|the} brings it up before you act.
generic.why: The guide applies to you now, and waiting leaves the problem in place.
generic.mis: Someone else will raise it if it matters.

overcaution.text: Shut down the whole area until every material has been sorted and every leak repaired.
overcaution.why: The concern is specific. Shutting everything down delays work that safe areas can keep doing.
overcaution.mis: Any waste problem means stopping everything.

setup: You have leftover cleaning solution. Its label restricts disposal to trained staff using product-specific instructions. You need their help.

steps.text: Keep the labeled container secured without opening it
Report the product and container details to trained staff
Wait for trained staff to arrange approved disposal

rel: Keep the container secured while you report it.
Trained staff need the product details before arranging disposal.
Record confirmation only after disposal is completed.
process.lesson: Secure, report, let trained staff handle disposal, and record confirmation.

title: Resource reminders
intro: You are checking a reminder sheet before it is posted in the supply room.
prompt: Which line gives advice that wastes resources?
doc.lesson: Use product-specific disposal instructions, report leaks, and avoid unused power.

lines.text: Keep chemical leftovers secured for trained staff to dispose of under the product instructions.
lines.fine: Keeps chemicals out of the water.

bad.text: Rinse leftover chemicals down the sink with plenty of water.
bad.why: Dilution does not stop chemicals from reaching the drain.

lines.text: Report leaks to maintenance as soon as you see them.

bad.text: Ignore a small leak, since it only drips a little.
bad.why: A steady drip wastes a lot of water over days.

lines.text: Turn off lights and equipment in rooms you are leaving empty.

bad.text: Leave lights on in empty rooms so the next person does not need to turn them on.
bad.why: The power is wasted for as long as the room is empty.

lines.text: Keep clean packing material for reuse.

review.notes: Everyday sustainable practices only; no environmental regulation is cited. Tiers: chemical disposal, leaks, recycling, power, reuse.
